utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Margetts, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Savkic, I would like to remind you -- well, you're getting used to it already, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Margetts, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, on the evening of the 16th of May, 1992, did you discuss with Rade Bjelanovic the cleansing operations that had been conducted by the police subordinated to him during the course of that day?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, this is a very serious insinuation, and in order to be consistent with everything that I have said so far, the answer absolutely is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you referred to my question as "a very serious insinuation." Why did you refer to my question in that manner?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, let's be just -- if I ask someone whether he killed another person, that could be understood. There's no need for an explanation of this witness that this is a serious insinuation. The question, as such, leaves it entirely open that Mr. Savkic would have had knowledge and would have discussed these kind of matters. So please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, I'd like to produce the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: In fact, it's two exhibits, and if they could be distributed. They're not in the tabs. And they're both dated 16 May 1992, and they are both reports submitted to the commander of the police station Milici, and they're both authored by Milan Bacic. The distinguishing feature is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can you just wait, please, until we've got a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I'm informed that you do have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't realise it was the documents handed out yesterday. Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The distinguishing feature, for the purpose of the registrar, is the introductory paragraph. One of these duty reports refers to the author having taken over duty at 0700 hours, and the other one refers to having taken over duty at 15, being a reference to 1500 hours. So if the one where the duty was taken over at 0700 hours could be marked with the first number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be P1069, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether I -- yes, my confusion is that I've got two copies, both 1500 hours and -- yes, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, you may see that the report for the one that refers to 0700 hours commences with the item "patrols," whereas the report for 1500 hours commences with the item "parties." Yes, Your Honour, and also my case manager has helpfully pointed out that the 0700 hours document is marked with the B/C/S -- the stamp on the B/C/S 01782489, and the original for the 1500 hours is marked with the stamp 01782488. Your Honour, may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, documents so similar need a moment of attention so that -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you'll see in the documents before you that this is a report submitted by a subordinate officer to Rade Bjelanovic, and it states on both of them that -- in the section referred to as "patrols," that "ciscenje terena" - in the B/C/S - was conducted by the police on the 16th of May, 1992. And during the course of your evidence in chief you pointed out on numerous occasions your close affiliation with Mr. Bjelanovic. And one -- in response to one answer -- one question, you said that Mr. Bjelanovic came every evening, or in most cases, and you exchanged information. It is the case, isn't it, Mr. Savkic, that on the evening of the 16th of May, 1992, you discussed with Mr. Bjelanovic, these "ciscenje terena" operations.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, the question -- the person who submitted the report is a person whom I don't know. On the 16th of May, 1992 - this is already a historical fact and time - fierce battles were being waged on the road from Derventa towards the mine in an attempt to return hijacked or kidnapped passengers from hijacked buses and trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, I must stop you there. We're not talking about those incidents; we're talking about the "ciscenje" operations conducted by the police. And as your evidence in chief demonstrates, the hijacking of the buses took place on the 21st of May. This is a very specific day. If you'd like, I can give you a very specific time that I'm interested in the "ciscenje" operations. The fact, you discussed with Mr. Bjelanovic the "ciscenje" operations, that took place in Zaklopaca between 1400 -- between 1600 and 1800 on the 16th of May, 1992, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, this is a construction by the Prosecutor on the 21st. I can prove it's just a construction. It's all absolutely incorrect. On the 21st - we can check in our transcript. You will see that this is an ambush. This has nothing to do with this date. You can conclude, based on documents, that we're talking about widespread fighting from Derventa towards Milici, and that it's about an attack on two Serb villages, Vasiljevic [phoen] and Ervici [phoen], during which fighting there was a total of five killed. This is stated in certain documents. You can find it also in Ivanica's book, but it's a generally known fact and there exists -- I mean, when you're talking about cleansing the terrain, we're speaking about these villages that were attacked and it was an attempt to re-take that territory. And when we're talking about that area towards the mine, these two documents, if they are legal, actually indicate that the police at that point in time -- and now that we're mentioning Mr. Zaklopaca, then according to all this information, and investigations are still underway, in the evening hours, then this is an absolute confirmation that the public security station police officers were out in the field where I said they were. And this is a historical fact. Everything can be proved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, the simple question was whether you discussed this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an answer to the question. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you purported to be providing an accurate history of events in Vlasenica to the Trial Chamber during the course of your examination-in-chief; however, you didn't mention in your evidence in chief that on Saturday, the 16th of May, 1992, over 60 Muslim men were killed in Zaklopaca. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Because he wasn't asked. I didn't object to that in relation to certain aspects yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Margetts, would you please point at the relevant questions where you would have expected the witness -- where you would have expected the witness to give a complete answer, including the facts you have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that wouldn't -- that's a task I haven't undertaken. I thought that it would be a matter understood by the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- in light of Your Honour's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can't expect the witness to give a complete -- I mean, events, a couple of weeks' area, where a lot of things happened during the day, you should at least be in a position to point at a question where this would have -- should have been part of a complete answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And I withdraw those comments, but I'll simply say this:

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: On Saturday, the 16th of May, 1992, over 60 Muslim men were killed in Zaklopaca. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do have relevant information. While reading the reports of survivors, and the numbers range from 60 upwards, the investigation was carried out by the IPTF. There was also an investigation by the competent prosecutor's office. At the moment, the cantonal prosecutor's office of Tuzla is conducting an investigation. I don't know what the information is that they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You referred to the investigation by the IPTF. In recent years, Mr. Milomir Milosevic was suspended from service at the Milici police station due to the fact that the IPTF concluded he had a role in this massacre in Zaklopaca. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You also referred to the investigations of the cantonal prosecutor's office in Tuzla. You are a suspect in those investigations, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever told me that I was a suspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: You also referred to the reports of survivors. At least two of them identify you as present, one of them identifying you as present as part of the militia that conducted the killings. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was never correct. There is a student of mine, Fikret Dugalic, many other students as well, just like all the citizens who came to Zaklopaca, with whom I talked. There wasn't a trace of any kind of strain in the relationship at any point. Nobody ever said anything like that to me. The person whose brothers, one or two brothers, were killed in this crime would not speak to somebody in such a friendly way, the way that person spoke. I state responsibly before this Tribunal that I found out about this two or three days later, and I can now in this time, in this moment, if I was connected -- if I were to be connected to a thousand polygraphs, I can guarantee that not a single one would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, whether these two people speak the truth or not is not part of the question. The question is just whether at least two persons identify you as being present. Right or wrong? That's the question: Are you aware of two people --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm hearing about this for the first time. I'm hearing it for the first time from this gentleman now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore you say: I spoke about the reports of survivors. I'm not aware of two people identifying you as being present. You hear for the first time about such statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm sure the Chamber will forgive the witness going into it in a little bit of detail. He's just been accused of mass murder. It's not altogether surprising --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Josse, his explanation is if he starts telling us there wasn't a trace of any of the persons, whose brother, et cetera, the Chamber has got no idea what he's talking about, so let's just stick to the questions. And of course, if you think it would be fair that these matters be further clarified, you have an ample opportunity, on the basis I interrupted the witness also, because he speaks about a lot of things the Chamber isn't aware of. Whether this is in the report of the survivors, whether these two people were the people who identified him as being present, or whether he thinks that these people might have identified him, the Chamber is not aware of it. So it doesn't add to it, but it's certainly -- if you have good grounds for further clarifying, or if you think it's important, of course you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I would like to change the topic, Mr. Savkic, and move to your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you have confronted the witness about two people identifying him as being present, which of course has some suggestive power. Is there any follow-up you're going to present to the Chamber in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason that that reference was made in the questions was in response to the witness's answer, to clarify -- he said he'd read statements of survivors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: We don't intend at this stage to proceed any further in relation to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but of course this is a -- more or less an allegation, to the extent that you said: There are good reasons to believe that you -- that you were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore, if such kind of allegation is made, and I'm now thinking about what I would call the Davidovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I please respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: He said that he'd read the statements of survivors, and I then asked him whether he'd read those statements that referred to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: We did not make an allegation that there were good reasons to believe he was there. What we said was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think that these survivors who say this had no good reasons, then we are slowly coming in the area, in the realm of what I would call the Davidovic issue. It's not exactly the same, but we are coming close to it, and therefore I think a warning is -- is justified. And at the same time, you leave the Chamber with question marks rather than with information. If you say, "Well, these two persons identifying Mr. Savkic as being there are not reliable witnesses of the event," then of course still the suggestion is there, and it's put to the witness and he says, "I do not know about it," then of course the Chamber would like to know what the good grounds -- what good grounds exist to put that to the witness as people identifying him as being present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can assure the Trial Chamber that we have good grounds for asking this witness as to whether he's read statements of the survivors that refer to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- and we have both of those statements with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you discuss the matter during the next break with the Defence to see whether by presenting -- even if these were only small portions, that at least you have good grounds to put this to the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's only time that prevents me from putting the full allegations to the witness. If I was allowed more time, I'd be more than happy to do it in open court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It is the Prosecution's position, having read the statements, that both of them appear to be highly reliable. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's say the following: This is a -- if there is a report -- if the witness says: I've read the report, then there should be a possibility, at least, to speak with Mr. Josse and to see whether you could agree on -- the mere fact -- no, Mr. Savkic, I'm talking to the parties at this moment. The mere fact that two people identify him is in those reports, just for the purposes I just mentioned, that Mr. Margetts had at least reason to put this to the witness who said that he had read the survivor reports, I take it that would be possible, wouldn't it, without going through the whole of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to think about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And of course, it is -- Your Honour, I -- this arose in the context of the witness referring to the cantonal investigation and raising it himself, and me -- and I only made a further inquiry in relation to that. Secondly, it arose in the context of him saying he read survivors' reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So I'd just like to put this in that context, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you were asked about the comments of Mr. Redzic, and in response to his comments regarding an alleged threat you made that tanks would come to Vlasenica and draw the borders in blood, you said that was nonsense. And you said: As for this attack from Milici or Zvornik, it's also a fact that neither place had a tank unit at that time. The relevant time being the time of the protocol, 11 April 1992. It's a fact, Mr. Savkic, that the tank unit, the 336th Motorised Brigade was stationed in Zvornik at that time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that brigade -- well, I've never heard about it. All I know is that in Milici and in Han Pijesak, at that period of time there had never been a single tank brigade there. We're talking about a tank, armoured brigade that Redzic is referring to, and you are referring to some kind of motorised brigade in Zvornik, apparently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, could you please point me at the day. Was it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- yes, Your Honour. It's page 20.540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I've got different page numbering. Do you have the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Which I understand would have been Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thursday was the -- just let me have a look --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: 26th January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 26th January. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Savkic, the statement that you made to the Trial Chamber that there wasn't a tank unit in Zvornik, that statement's incorrect, isn't it? Or, alternatively, you don't know whether there was or not, so your statement to the Trial Chamber was not based on any knowledge; it was just speculation on your behalf.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say specifically earlier on that there had never been one in Milici, but you mentioned a motorised brigade, but Redzic referred to an armoured brigade. And I never knew anything about a motorised brigade. They would go through the area, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, let me just read to you exactly what you said on the 26th when confronted with the allegations made by Mr. Redzic. You said: "It is an obvious nonsense. At that moment in Han Pijesak, there was not a single tank unit of the Yugoslav People's Army, not even in the reserve forces or in the rear where the infantry battalion was stationed. As for this attack from Milici or Zvornik, it's also a fact that neither place had a tank unit at that time and not only at that time." These are your literal words as they appear in the transcript. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can introduce tab 48, and if that could have an exhibit number. And also my case manager reminds me that the second exhibit presented this morning didn't receive the number, which I assume is P1070.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the report of the duty officer dated 16th May, 1992, referring to the 1500 hours commencement will be given P1070.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this -- I think the reference to tab 48 may have been mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps come up with --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, Your Honour. It's tab 45 I wish to refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then check, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1071, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1071, and that -- and that is a -- let me see what the description is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's a report from Commander Major General Savo Jankovic to the 17th Corps command, dated 9 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore the description changes as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, if you could look at paragraph 5 of that report, it states that: "A 336th Motorised Brigade tank, T-55, slipped off the road at Sapna bridge in the village of Celopek near Zvornik." Now, you made the distinction between an armoured brigade and the 336th Motorised Brigade. It's the fact that the 336th Motorised Brigade was formally known as the 4th Armoured Brigade and was a tank unit commanded by Dragan Obrenovic in Zvornik as at the time that Mr. Redzic alleges you said tanks were in the vicinity and could come to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Sapna area is on the road between Tuzla and Zvornik. Therefore, it has nothing whatsoever to do with Zvornik. The interpretation provided by the gentleman here, according to which in a motorised brigade there would be tanks and such-like, well motorised brigade is one thing -- it is true that they have tanks, but a tank or an armoured brigade is totally different because they only have tanks. And it is quite clear here that we are not talking about Zvornik, but we are talking about a totally different direction. And it has nothing to do with the Zvornik-Milici line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could move to another topic, and that is Exhibit D130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just put the following to the witness. The whole issue, Mr. Savkic, arose from the -- the words of Mr. Redzic, and he said that the Serbs had tanks ready. And you say that's all nonsense because there were no tank units. Now, that's not what Mr. Redzic said. He didn't say "there were tank units," but "there were tanks." Now Mr. Margetts puts it to you that even if this would not be a tank unit, that at least a tank was nearby. And to that aspect -- to that extent your statement that it's all nonsense, he puts it to you that it is not nonsense because there was at least, as he referred to, one tank. That's the issue. We're not talking about organisation of the army, about whether the unit was full of tanks or -- we're just talking about an allegation made by Mr. Redzic that tanks were ready. You said it's nonsense because there were no tank units, suggesting that there were no tanks either. And now Mr. Margetts confronts you with at least one tank at least mentioned in a report. Yes, could you please respond to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, apart from saying that it was utter nonsense, I also added -- and I don't suppose that he had mentioned that at all. That's my first point. And the second point is that at this moment in time, due to the withdrawal of all the army units of the JNA from Croatia, et cetera, what I said in my comment was that when we talk about Milici, Zvornik, and the entire area, columns of JNA army soldiers from Croatia were going through. This was what may have been mentioned at this trial for reasons having to do with the fact that many units transited through the area at the time. And it can be seen that this column was coming from the direction of Tuzla. It is quite clear, it is crystal clear, on the basis of this order. And that's what it says here in the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has nothing to do with Zvornik, nothing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you presented an exhibit to the Trial Chamber, it's Exhibit D130, and it was a list of policemen who were invited for training in Sarajevo. And you told the Trial Chamber that of the 448 names, according to your analysis, 313 were Muslims and 135 were Croats. We have taken the opportunity to review that list with an expert demographer. The fact is, Mr. Savkic, that at least 55 of the people on that list are certainly Serbs. Your evidence was misleading and incorrect, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're misquoting me totally. Could we go back to the transcript, and in that case you will see that I said specifically that on the basis of the list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Go back to the transcript. Mr. Margetts, the date was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It was on the Thursday, the 26th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we're talking about the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And the relevant portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have text, that's easier for me to get that on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Okay. I can read that to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: "135 were non-Muslims --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think "135" would be a good thing to search for. Yes. You said the following, Mr. Savkic -- you said: "On the last page, it is to do the maths and see that out of 313 candidates that met the requirements, 135 were non-Muslims -- actually, those were all Croats. The rest were all Muslims. However, I have to clarify one more thing --" and -- and then the word is not -- "and do a reality check. During that period - and not only during that period of time - to send Serbs to Zagreb for training, given the well-known developments would have been crazy." So these were your words. Now Mr. Margetts puts it to you that, according to people he consulted, that there are at least 55 Serbs on that list. He confronts you with that and he asks you for a comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But he said out of those 400-something - everything on the list, that is - and on my statement it says clearly out of 313 of those invited. That's what you just read out. Those who went on the course, 135 were not Muslims and the others were all Muslims. You've only just read it out, so the gentleman is absolutely and totally wrong then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But -- Mr. Margetts, perhaps in your next question you could clarify this issue. It seems that the witness says: I'm starting from 313, I did not count them all. And you started a longer list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the words that the witness spoke were the following: "135 from the list were non-Muslims." He says --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Do it to the witness, not to the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I'm saying is this: Is that the question that the Court has put to Mr. Savkic does not equate --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. This is not an argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Margetts --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: -- cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Josse invites you to put to the witness what he said. And by putting questions to him you'll certainly be able to further clarify the matter. Could I have the list in front of me. That's D130, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you said the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, first of all the registrar draws my attention that where you said "D130," you most likely wanted to refer to D133. Is that correct? D130 to be a -- no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think a mistake was made by me. We are talking about tab 9. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Tab 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 16. Tab 16 is D133.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honour. D133 is the document I wish to refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you told the Trial Chamber, reviewing the document D133: "It's easy to do the maths and see that out of 313 candidates that met the requirements, 135 were non-Muslims -- actually, those were all Croats. The rest were all Muslims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Margetts, the issue seems to be that -- that Mr. Josse asked about the list. "The documents, for the purpose of translation, have been split up, but as you understand it the list of 448 names was effectively attached to the letter from Mr. Srebrenikovic." So there we start discussing a list of 448 people. Then later on, Mr. Josse asked: "But what was the result of your research through these 448 names? I think you've marked it, haven't you, on the very last page, the very last page, of the bundle?" And then the witness continued: "Yes, yes. On the last page, it is to do the maths and see that out of 313 candidates --" so as a matter of fact that met the requirements -- "135 were non-Muslims ..." Now, if I add 313 with 135, that brings me to 448. So therefore, I am a bit surprised that the 135 are now deducted from the 313 instead of deducted from the 448. But most important is, Mr. Savkic, that this list you seem to have analysed, and where it says at the very last page 330, 135, we are talking about that list. One of the things I would be inclined to do is to count them and to see whether we have a list of 313 or a list of 448.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we are all in agreement that it's a list of 448.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse, are we in agreement that the list is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, secondly, may I say this: I think we're all in agreement that it's the witness's handwritten annotation on that list which makes the distinction between 313 and 135.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now his testimony -- but let's first ask you. From your answer it appears that one could not possibly -- it would be very illogical - as you said, crazy - to have any Serbs on that list. Now, we have a list of 448 people. You made a distinction between 313 on the one-hand side and 135 remaining. Please explain now to us whether there were -- no, Mr. Savkic. Please, one moment. A bit impatient. Explain to us, are there any Serbs on this list as you saw it, where both counsel agreed that it's a list of 448 people? Are there any Serbs on that list? Yes, could you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this list, out of 430-something people, there were some Serbs; I'm not arguing with that, Mr. President. But in case the translation into English is correct, what I'm referring to is people who were admitted. They were surrounded by Mr. Srebrenikovic, and those people who went through that medical training, this 313 who passed -- or rather, their names were underlined there, and 135 Muslims. I can't tell for sure on the basis of every single name, but almost all of them, both this 135, are Croats, and I said that out of this 135 there may be some Serbs and it would have been a lunacy to send a Serb to Zagreb at that time; that's what I'm saying. You've read it out, but perhaps your translation is bad or whatever. 313 admitted and 135 were non-Muslims, and then I added what I added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So your testimony is that, by coincidence, the number of 135 is also the number that -- of people that were not selected. But did I understand -- but I have to verify that. Did I understand you well when you said that this was all a secret operation of people being trained in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From previous SDA orders, you could have seen that initially it was a covert operation. On the basis of this list, you can see that out of 435 individuals, those whose names are not encircled, who supposedly failed that medical, you will see that they're, all of them, Serbs. And let me stress once again, out of 313 whose names are indicated as having gone through this training, 135 are non-Muslims, mostly Croats, on the basis of their names and the geographical area of provenance. Just look at the names which are not marked, not encircled. Out of these 434 [as interpreted] you will see that all of those names are Serb names, almost all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So now the present situation is that the witness says that those names that are not encircled, that those are the Serbs. I don't know, Mr. Margetts, whether it's possible for you to seek verification of this. But at least, Mr. Savkic, if this was such a secret operation, why would there be so many Serbs as candidates on that list? I mean, if you want to keep something secret, then you would not expect quite a number of Serbs to be on that list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should ask candidates from the ranks of the Serbs whether they were even invited to that medical at all, whether they went, and for what reason they failed. How come only the Serbs failed? If indeed there had been a kind of medical there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes -- well, of course, that's still to be seen. Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, a witness who has given evidence -- well, not given evidence, but evidence from this witness has been produced as an expert report, KRAJ 618, has prepared a demographic study. We don't have a B/C/S copy, so we're not in a position to put the entire document to the witness; however, we would like to introduce that as an exhibit. And it appears at tab 46 of the bundle, and if that could be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 46 will be P1072, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object. This is rebuttal evidence, in effect. I mean, it's not an original document; it's been prepared for the purpose of these proceedings. We've got no opportunity to challenge this; it's rebuttal evidence in another guise, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will have to decide on whether or not it will admit this evidence at this stage of the proceedings. Mr. Margetts, is there any -- did you intend to confront the witness with this expert report or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've already confronted the witness with one of the major conclusions set out in this report, which is that at least 55 of the persons were certainly Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness now gave us his explanation that -- which was certainly not clear in the beginning, that the circled persons were the ones selected and the non-circled persons were Serbs not selected. That at least was not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I accept, for what it's worth, I didn't bring the evidence out terribly well, having looked at the transcripts, excuse me making that comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you revisit the matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'm going to do that, Your Honour, but could I say, in fairness, this bundle was handed to us yesterday, and I didn't look at these particular documents overnight, but this is an expert report that is served as the witness is giving evidence. I mean, the Prosecution is at least under a duty to draw it to my attention and say: In the bundle of exhibits is an expert report, you need to consider it. This really is not the way to conduct cross-examination, I submit firmly and strongly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, Mr. Josse blames you for not having drawn his attention to presenting a -- well, a report which was drafted as an expert report since the witness has given his testimony last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's self-evident that this is an expert report. Mr. Josse had the opportunity to review his bundle. It would have been condescending to explain to him what that was; it's obvious on its face.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, does it appear on the index? Because I can imagine that if I were Defence counsel, I would first have a look at the index to see whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: It's described as a "Declaration on ethnic distribution of selected names in BiH population census, 31 March, 1991."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I make this observation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That's not a complete description. "Dated 26th January, 2006."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I make this observation, Your Honour? My learned friend knows that, unusually, I actually went through the exhibit up to tab 41 on Friday when they were handed out. He knows that because I sent Mr. Harmon an e-mail, making various observations about that bundle. 42 onwards was handed out yesterday. As I've already said, I didn't look at those overnight. Whether I should have done is neither here nor there. Generally, the Defence can't complain about the way that these documents are dealt with in cross-examination - it's perhaps a matter for another day - but this is completely different, as I've already submitted, and it has no part at all in the cross-examination of a witness. The assertions contained in it my learned friend put boldly, I didn't object to that, that an expert says X, Y, and Z. What then happened thereafter, confusion, well, that's neither here nor there, but this is really a radical departure from the Rules on a matter that's going to need, in my submission, closer and further analysis in due course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid the Rules are not very explicit in this respect, Mr. Josse, so the Chamber will have to find its way through the Rules to see how to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we say this: That we're more than happy for Mr. Josse to take his time to consider that exhibit and then to put his position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The parties are -- I do see that at least -- and that's the first step, perhaps, we should take is to compare whether -- to look at whether this report -- I'll do it over the next break and -- because we might not finish before the first break. Mr. Margetts, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, is the case in fact that nine of the Serbs who were listed as being candidates for this training went on to serve in one of the leading police units for the Republika Srpska, the special forces attached to the Ministry of the Interior, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the text in Serbian here; I have it in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you talking about the expert report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this information is not contained in the expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You were asked whether -- let me first -- if you said: "I have only the text in English," what document were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The witness has the declaration open before him; I can see that from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The declaration -- yes. Don't worry about that. That's another matter. The question is put to you whether -- whether nine of the Serbs you find on the list -- and I'm changing the question slightly, Mr. Margetts, because "selected" and "selection," as the witness told us, goes in two stages. That is a list of selected people, and then they had to undergo a medical examination, and then the selection was refined on the basis of that, if at all there was a medical examination. So let's talk about Serbs on the list. Are you aware that nine of the Serbs who appear on this list went on to serve in one of the -- that doesn't appear on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the police units for the Republika Srpska. That's the question. And it was specified as being the special forces attached to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Savkic is again referring to the declaration before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Savkic, put the declaration, the English text, aside; that's not relevant at this moment. Are you aware that nine of the persons on this list served later on in the Republika Srpska police force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall any Serb first or last name from that list right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could refer now to tab 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tab 47, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And that's a list of members of the special detachment of the Ministry of the Interior. That's the elite special force attachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And if that could be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 47 would be P1073, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you are aware of the elite special force unit attached to the Ministry of the Interior, Republika Srpska, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Special unit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, look at the list before you. On the first page, look at number 13, Miroslav Subotic. On the second page, look at number 35, Mladen Kusmuk?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, would it be possible to refer to D133 as well so we can compare the names and see whether they actually appear on the list, and of course for the Chamber also important to see whether they are encircled, yes or no. So first one being 13, Miroslav Subotic, and we find him on the other list where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Number 50, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 50. Yes, that's the first name. The second one, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Is number 35 on the Exhibit P1073, which is Mladen Kusmuk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- 35, Mladen Kusmuk -- and we find him on the other list at? That's D133, we find him --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: And we find him -- Your Honour, I have to at this stage say I haven't formed that reconciliation. I apologise for not having done that prior to the next exhibit. I can tell you that number 35 is number 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, number 115. Mladen Kusmuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next one is 36, Stojan Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Number 36, Stojan Stojanovic, yes. On the other list, to appear on --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- part of the list. At number 113, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 113, top -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next is number 49 on D1073 [sic], and that is Milorad Pavlica. And he appears at number 179 on D133. The next name on D1073 [sic] is Predrag Mizdrak, and that's at number 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps complete that during the next break and at this moment focus on 179 and perhaps -- Mr. Savkic, we'll further complete this matter, but you explained to us that all the Serbs were eliminated from that list and you said those ones circled were the ones selected, the other ones not selected. Now, if you look at the list for Milorad Pavlica, he seems to be selected and he appears on the list of special police forces. He, at least as you explained to us, was one of the selected ones and Mr. Margetts puts it to you that he's a Serb, and you said you couldn't expect a Serb to undergo this training, it would be crazy. Could you explain or could you assist the Chamber in reconciling this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, gentlemen. I said when I -- at the end of my statement about that, that there were 145 [as interpreted] Muslims. Judging by the names and the fact that they're similar, I don't know if there are geographical things in common, but they were mostly Croats. Those that were chosen, and I said that and I stand by that, for a Serb to go and attend a course in Zagreb at that time was absolute nonsense. In the same way, this gentleman who was in the special unit in June doesn't actually mean that he did go to Zagreb and complete that training. There's nothing there indicating anything like that. Judging by the last names, I can tell that some people are from Romanija and other places. I think that at that time there was no Serb who would actually go to Zagreb. I think that the clarification is the only logical one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're rather concentrating on facts than logic, Mr. Savkic, and please keep that in mind because human beings do not always behave in accordance with logic. Please proceed, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, focussing -- sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, focussing on Milorad Pavlica, you said you could conclude from geographic location that people were Croats. Milorad Pavlica came from Kupres. Kupres is a majority Serbian municipality, or was at the time of this document, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that the Serbs were a majority in Kupres. Specifically Pavlica, that name, if you look at how many Pavlicas there are in Rijeka - there's a football player - and they're all Croats. So I did say it quite specifically, not Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Well, let's then look, Mr. Savkic, at Slobodan Bogdanovic, one of the people on the list. It is the case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts, please, numbers. On the one list and on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Number 204. And, Your Honour, I'm not sure that he's a member of the special unit. I'm just referring to him on the list of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Number 204 on the list presented with D133, Mr. Slobodan Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: It's the case, Mr. Savkic, that in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991, there was no Croat named Slobodan Bogdanovic. Of the 14 Slobodan Bogdanovics that lived in Bosnia, ten were Serbs and four were Yugoslavs. But you came to this Trial Chamber and said: On the basis of the names, I can conclude that 135 people who were non-Muslims were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness meanwhile admitted, Mr. Margetts, that there may have been Serbs on that list, but they were not -- you remember the discussion of the 448 to start with or the 313. So I don't think at this moment it's the testimony of the witness that no Serb or no Serb name appears on this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. If I may move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, yesterday when I spoke to you about your service in the military, you explained to me that although in your military booklet it states that your service commenced on the 6th of April, in fact it commenced later. You said: "I didn't say that it was from the 6th of April that I was in any military unit. What I said was that our military booklets had either the date 4th of April or the 6th of April written down in them." Now, Mr. Savkic, it's the same for the Muslim members of the military as well. Their military booklets record the date that war was declared, but that doesn't mean that they were serving in a military unit at that time, does it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which Muslims do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The Muslims mobilised in April of 1992 who then served in the ABiH army may have a military booklet that records that their date of service started, for instance, on the 5th of April, 1992, but it doesn't mean that they were serving in a unit at that time; exactly the same as the situation for the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible. But there are documents, and we'll see them later, where you have that as recorded -- being recorded before April 1st. Even in December 1991, there were Muslims who were in the military formations, paramilitary formations. At that -- you have that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you came before this Court and you brought a Muslim military booklet, and you represented to this Trial Chamber that the date of service of 5th of April, 1992, meant that the 16th Muslim Brigade existed at that time. That is a misrepresentation, and you well know that the 16th Muslim Brigade did not exist until early June 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the booklet, it states clearly that this is not Territorial Defence but a military unit. And these are the dates when the person was mobilised into the Territorial Defence, and it's according to the law and to the constitution, regulations that were valid at that time. And there is a major difference there. This is what it states in the booklet, so it was a combat unit, not a TO unit, which was the case with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: But it was not the 16th Muslim Brigade, was it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the booklet, it said "16th Muslim Brigade." There is an original still that can be seen, and this was something that did -- was not written only on the military booklet. It didn't state "Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina," but it stated "the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I didn't ask you what was stated in the booklet. I said: The booklet does not show that the 16th Muslim Brigade existed as at the time the individual's war service commenced, exactly the same as a Drina Corps booklet would not show that the date that the Drina Corps existed was the date that the person started their war service. Consequently, Mr. Savkic, you have misrepresented that document to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not focus that much on misrepresentation. Mr. Savkic, Mr. Margetts says if in your military booklets a date is entered, not because one took up active service at that moment but for other reasons - for example, that was the beginning of the war - the same is true for Muslims. So from that military booklet we could not conclude, as you apparently did, that the 16th Muslim Brigade existed at that time. And, Mr. Margetts, do we have any further information about the establishment of the 16th Muslim Brigade? Because that's what the Chamber, of course, would like to see then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have an exhibit prepared in regard to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that would certainly have assisted the Chamber, because even if a military booklet could have been filled in on the basis of an assumption rather than on facts, at the same time one could not exclude that it's filled in on the basis of facts rather than assumptions. So therefore, to clarify this matter, the Chamber would like then to see any further evidence about the establishment of the 16th Muslim Brigade, because you said at the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. In fact, the 8th of June, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- is the date that we say that brigade is formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You must have a reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why not present that to the Chamber so that we can better assess whether that reason is a reasonable reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will endeavour to do so at the break, to prepare the exhibit and present it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And of course you could have imagined before and if want to confront the witness with a similar system, and especially in relation to the 16th Muslim Brigade, of course the Chamber would very much like to determine this matter on the basis of facts and documents rather than on this, could I say, fluid exchange of positions in relation of interpretation of documents. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- when I say, "Please proceed," I also see that it's 10.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: One short matter, Your Honour, and then I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, you told the Trial Chamber that there was no expanded Presidency, and "none of us -" and at the time you were referring to the deputies - "were ever told of an expanded Presidency and it didn't exist. There was no expanded Presidency at that time. I had never heard of such a thing as an extended Presidency." Mr. Savkic, you attended the 22nd Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly in Zvornik between the 22nd and the 24th of November, 1992, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember attending a session in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: At that session, Mr. Milan Trbojevic stated: "First of all we have set up a para-system of power. The public and so-called legal war state Presidency is a body that does not exist in the constitution. War commissioners which are working in the field do not exist in an organ in any country, according to the constitution and the law. Thus we can conclude that a para-government might be existing from top of the state all the way down to the level of municipalities because we have no information whether it was misused." Mr. Trbojevic stated quite clearly to all of the persons present that -- that you had set up a para-system of power with the so-called "legal" war state Presidency. Correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Trbojevic is saying there when he's talking about an expanded Presidency. If he considers the Presidency to be Ms. Biljana Plavsic, Mr. Koljevic, and that that's extended by the president, Radovan Karadzic, well in that sense, that's perhaps it. Everything else that he says, to tell you the truth, I don't understand anything. War commissioner never - at least, not in the units that I was in - never existed. I don't even know what a war commissioner is. I know it from films on the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The subject of the discussion at that Assembly session was the war state Presidency, that is the -- a Presidency in its expanded composition, as defined by the decision of June 1992 to amend the constitution to allow for this expanded Presidency. Is it your evidence to this Trial Chamber that during the course of that session you did not understand that the subject of the matter was the expanded Presidency?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's the meeting we're talking about, the basic topic was the resignation of the head of government, Mr. Zekic, if that's the meeting we're talking about. If not, I have not the foggiest of what it is all about, what Trbojevic as a legal expert was on about. I do remember a meeting in Zvornik, on the occasion of which the president of the government, the head of government, Mr. Djeric, handed in his resignation. I know that it was the main topic, and that was when the government changed. I believe that's the meeting we are talking about. I remember nothing else. As far as I am concerned, as a new deputy, the way I could see it, it was the crux of the matter. It was the most important thing discussed there. If that's the meeting you are talking about, and that's the only one I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, subject to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I now receive French - a nice language - on channel 4, but I'd prefer to have English. Could you please repeat what you just said, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes the questions that I intended to ask this witness; however, I note that issues have arisen during the course of the cross-examination in regard to a further exhibit relating to the 16th Muslimanski Brigade and also in regard to discussions that we'll be having at the break with the Defence in regard to the statements relating to the incidents at Zaklopaca. So subject to those two issues, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break -- unfortunately, Mr. Savkic, we were not able to finish during the first session, but we most likely will do in the second session, which will start at 5 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, I'm on my feet, Your Honour, so perhaps I could deal with it. First of all, in relation to the Zaklopaca incident, if I can call it that, as I understand what I've been told by the Prosecution, they are prepared to accept -- the question they asked the witness was whether he had seen statements which implicated him. His answer was, No. And they are prepared to stop at that. I will be corrected if I am wrong. If that is the position, then I -- Defence are content with the state of the evidence so far as that issue is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's verify it. Is Mr. Josse's understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then that matter is settled.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Whilst I am on my feet, so far as the demographic statement is concerned, if I can call it that, Your Honour, I've had an opportunity to reflect on this. Could I make it absolutely clear - and I've only been able to speak briefly to Mr. Stewart - were this to happen again, we'd reserve our position to take the point that I've begun to take in relation to notice, whether it's the right thing to do, and so on and so forth. However, the witness has accepted, in effect, what's contained within the demographer's report. He said that the list has a significant number of Serbian names upon it. So when it comes to discussion of admission of documents, I will not object to the admission of that report. I hope that's helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, it may have created, but I have not yet looked at it in much detail ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In order to fully understand the -- Mr. Margetts, you said something about nine Serbs. I see seven combinations of names in this report, none of them being the name listed under 179, Milorad Pavlica. Because if we would have to -- the witness told us that the ones with the numbers encircled were the ones who were selected, and the other ones were not selected, and he told us that all Serbs were among the not selected. Number 179, you mentioned as a person who later on, I think, served in the special police force of Republika Srpska, but that name does not appear in the expert report as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe if I could address the expert report and what it seeks to set out in the table -- is it table 1 you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This expert -- I'm talking about the declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, let me just have a look there. I didn't see it in the full --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The expert report does not draw a distinction between those names that were circled and those names that were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But let's just now see whether I find this -- this Milorad Pavlica, which you refer to as someone serving later on at the Republika Srpska police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is not identified by the expert or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let me -- could you please assist me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just address the declaration for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The declaration was prepared on the basis, first of all, scrutiny of the list was undertaken by persons from the region who identified names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- they thought looked like Serb names. That list of names was referred to the expert, who then performed a demographic analysis of those names. The annexure to the declaration sets out the results of that demographic analysis, where it was verified those individuals were Serb. And then furthermore, because of the methodology that had been referred to in the witness's evidence in chief, namely in circumstances of ambiguity, the region that they were from was referred to, a special table was prepared listing those persons who in all of Bosnia-Herzegovina were either -- all of the persons by that name were either only Serbs or Serbs and Yugoslavs, and that's the -- that's what table 1 is, to address the issue of methodology. So the issue of the names that were circled or not circled is not addressed in the declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then of course in order to better understand the testimony of the witness, because the witness said those names where there's a circle around the number, those were selected, and the ones not circled are the Serbs that were left out, so therefore, it would make sense to look, to compare all the 58 names appearing in the expert report and see whether there -- these names are -- and that's not a very complicated job to do, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, "These names are ..." Your Honour stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether these names are encircled - yes or no - on the other list. Because the explanation of the witness was that those names not circled were the people not selected. And as he said, this was the way to -- one would not select Serbs on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I make it clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I've said this already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: This, in part, was my fault because I didn't adduce the evidence terribly well when I dealt with the witness in chief; let me readily accept that. And that of course has made the Prosecution tab 46 somewhat redundant, and that of course is not their fault, as I have already conceded. I was going to ask the witness a few more questions about this in re-examination. Mr. Karganovic has attempted to do a very quick and rough-and-ready analysis, but a more detailed one might require somewhat more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at least, Mr. Margetts, if you look at the first ten, they're all non-circled and therefore non-selected candidates, from what I understand. And also the -- let's wait and see what Mr. Josse --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can just on this analysis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- in the moments that I've just had while my learned friend was talking, I've identified that number 30 in the declaration, Mladen Popovic, is number 264 on the list. He is both a Serb and circled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We found the 179 one as well. So it seems not to be a complete explanation, but let's first -- everyone can use this time to compare the 58 and look at it. Even the legal officer who is assisting the Chamber might do some useful work in this if he has got the relevant documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- also I -- obviously I apologise again for not having a reconciliation performed between Exhibit D133 and P1073. I can read a reconciliation into the record that has been provided to me at the break, if that's helpful. That is, the numbers that appear on D133 reconciled with the numbers that appear on the list of the members of the special unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then I especially -- if you do that, how many would you have on both lists?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I've got nine names, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've got nine names. I'm mainly interested in the -- if you please do that very slowly so that no mistakes appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Would you like to check the names on both exhibits as I read, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would -- if you have the -- yes. If you would have the -- first mention the number in the special units list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That special unit list was D --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: P1073, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. P1073. And then second, the corresponding number in the list of candidates, D133.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The first number is number 13 on P1073, and that name appears at number 50 in D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Miroslav Subotic, not encircled. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Next is number 35 in P1073. That appears as number 115 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 115 being Mladen Kusmuk, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next number is number 36 on P1073, and number 113 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's Stojan Stojanovic, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Next is number 49 on P1073 and number 179 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Milorad Pavlica, who is encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next is number 85 on P1073 and number 395 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 395 being Predrag Mizdrak, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next number is number 98 on P1073 and number 297 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 297 being Dragisa Kuskuk, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: There's also a notation here that Kuskuk should be Kusmuk, so there may be a typo in one of the lists --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, or it's not the same person. We'll check that carefully on the basis of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Next, Your Honour, is 113 on P1073, which is 349 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 349 being Zoran Golijanin, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Then we have 127 on P1073, and that corresponds with 437 on D133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 437 being Mladen Rakicc, and surprisingly with double "c" at the end, not encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: The next is 136 on P1073, which corresponds to 301 on D133. That completes the list, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: 1, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1, you said, and that's Radomir Kovac, or Kovak, not encircled. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one further issue not related to this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Just before -- on that. In the light of that analysis, for the avoidance of any doubt, I don't intend to re-examine the witness in the course -- I just need to make that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least now it's clear to what extent there's correspondence also to circles around the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The unrelated issue, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was before the break I indicated that I would present an exhibit in respect of the date of formation of the 16th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 16th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: -- Muslim Brigade. I've had discussions in relation to that, and I'd like to inform Your Honour that we don't intend to present an exhibit, and the reason for this is as follows: The basis that we had for the date of the formation of the brigade was on the basis of, first, an expert military opinion on the formation of ABiH units and the transformation of TO to units, and the material related to that generally rather than any specific document relating to the 16th Muslim Brigade. Second, it was payment lists, whilst indicating the 8th of June as the first date for the members that unit, doesn't specifically say that the 8th of June is the first date that that brigade existed. But when read with an expert opinion and the further document that we have -- and the further document is this, it's a book which actually expressly states that the 16th Muslim Brigade was formed at that date in early June with the transformation of the TO. So if we were to present an exhibit, it would merely be a book, although -- so we don't wish to do that. But our opinion is based on a range of factors and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. All factors not being in evidence at this moment. At the same time I see that you have examined the witness on the issue of whether a date in the military booklet would be sufficient -- a sufficient indication of the existence of the unit which is mentioned in that same booklet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you do not take it for granted -- you thus have drawn the attention of the Chamber to the fact that it's not self-explanatory that if a date appears, that the unit already existed on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That [inaudible] the question. There's just one more thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it would have been better, as a matter of fact, Mr. Margetts, if you would have left it to that and say: We put questions to the witness, we had good reasons to do so, but we're not going to further pursue the matter. Because now it's a bit suggestive -- you say that at least your interpretation would find support in a book which you're not going to present, et cetera, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The reason I didn't object, Your Honour, is with respect to all Your Honours, I'm sure this Court is well able to distinguish matters which are in evidence and those which are in argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not without reason that I started saying: "That's all not in evidence."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Absolutely. That reassured the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Josse, you will appreciate that the Chamber, by giving this gentle guidance to Mr. Margetts even would like to be released from even having to consider that question in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I suppose there may be days where I will be a little less charitable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: I thank my learned friend for his response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Josse, are you ready to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, Mr. Josse will re-examine you. Mr. Josse, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Savkic, have a look, please, at tab 5 in the Prosecution bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: When this document was put to you by my learned friend Mr. Margetts, you said, in terms, that it was a forgery. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And you at one point told the Chamber that it may have been prepared by criminals that had been persecuting you all your life, especially during the war. Who did you have in mind and what did you mean by that answer?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say in the course of the war, but I said those that had persecuted me throughout my life. What I meant specifically was this: This is a forgery. There is not a signature of mine anywhere. And I also explained that those were people who probably wished to cover up some kind of transaction in connection with the -- with tax evasion. And I had problems with them also between 1998 and 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Can you be more specific as to who these criminal elements are?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV SAVKIC [Resumed]
